message.abstract: <jats:p><jats:italic>Context</jats:italic>. It has been proposed that the distinct formation and evolutionary pathways of exoplanets and brown dwarfs may affect the chemical and isotopic content of their atmospheres. Recent work has indeed shown differences in the<jats:sup>12</jats:sup>C/<jats:sup>13</jats:sup>C isotope ratio, which have provisionally been attributed to the top-down formation of brown dwarfs and the core accretion pathway of super-Jupiters.</jats:p><jats:p><jats:italic>Aims</jats:italic>. The ESO SupJup Survey is aimed at disentangling the formation pathways of isolated brown dwarfs and planetary-mass companions using chemical and isotopic tracers. The survey utilises high-resolution spectroscopy with the recently upgraded CRyogenic high-resolution InfraRed Echelle Spectrograph (CRIRES<jats:sup>+</jats:sup>) at the Very Large Telescope, covering a total of 49 targets. Here, we present the first results of this survey: an atmospheric characterisation of DENIS J0255-4700, an isolated brown dwarf near the L-T transition.</jats:p><jats:p><jats:italic>Methods</jats:italic>. We analysed its observed CRIRES<jats:sup>+</jats:sup><jats:italic>K</jats:italic>-band spectrum using an atmospheric retrieval framework in which the radiative transfer code<jats:monospace>petitRADTRANS</jats:monospace>was coupled with the<jats:monospace>PyMultiNest</jats:monospace>sampling algorithm. Gaussian processes were employed to model inter-pixel correlations. In addition, we adopted an updated parameterisation of the pressure-temperature profile.</jats:p><jats:p><jats:italic>Results</jats:italic>. Abundances of CO, H<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O, CH<jats:sub>4</jats:sub>, and NH<jats:sub>3</jats:sub>were retrieved for this fast-rotating L-dwarf. The ExoMol H<jats:sub>2</jats:sub>O line list provides a significantly better fit than that of HITEMP. A free-chemistry retrieval is strongly favoured over equilibrium chemistry, caused by an under-abundance of CH<jats:sub>4</jats:sub>. The free-chemistry retrieval constrains a super-solar C/O-ratio of ~0.68 and a solar metallicity. We find tentative evidence (~3<jats:italic>σ</jats:italic>) for the presence of<jats:sup>13</jats:sup>CO, with a constraint on the isotopologue ratio of<jats:sup>12</jats:sup>CO/<jats:sup>13</jats:sup>CO = 184<jats:sub>−40</jats:sub><jats:sup>+61</jats:sup>and a lower limit of ≳97, which suggests a depletion of<jats:sup>13</jats:sup>C compared to the local interstellar medium (<jats:sup>12</jats:sup>C/<jats:sup>13</jats:sup>C ~ 68).</jats:p><jats:p><jats:italic>Conclusions</jats:italic>. High-resolution, high signal-to-noise<jats:italic>K</jats:italic>-band spectra provide an excellent means of constraining the chemistry and isotopic content of sub-stellar objects, which is the main objective of the ESO SupJup Survey.</jats:p>
title: The ESO SupJup Survey
